name: Remembrance of the Name (nām-sumiran)
method_summary: Inward, continuous remembrance of the Lord's Name (usually Rām or the name given by the guru), joined to the breath and held in the mind, in all activities; outward recitation on beads without the mind is rejected.

warnings.text: The rosary turns in the hand and the tongue in the mouth while the mind wanders in ten directions — this is not remembrance.

equivalents.note: Name-repetition, but the Sants stress the inward, mind-held remembrance over counted recitation.

name: Ajapā japa (the unrepeated repetition)
method_summary: In Sant usage: the Name continuing of itself with the breath, without tongue or beads, after long remembrance (a Nāth-derived notion adopted by Dādū and others).

name: The natural discipline (sahaj): every act as worship
method_summary: Living in constant awareness of the Lord without forced austerities: eyes open, going about as circumambulation, work as service, lying down as prostration; no closing of eyes, stopping of ears or mortification.
signs_of_progress: the Lord's form seen everywhere with open eyes (Kabīr)

warnings.text: Everyone speaks of sahaj but no one knows it: it is not ease or laxity.

name: Satsaṅg (company of the sants)
method_summary: Gathering with sants and devotees to sing their songs (bhajan), hear their words and the master's discourse; among Bāuls and Kartābhajās the ākhṛā and melā gatherings with sādhu-sevā.

warnings.text: Bad company (kusaṅg) undoes practice; know the sādhu by conduct, not dress.

name: Devotion to the guru
method_summary: Honouring the true guru as the giver of the Name, above or equal to God: surrender, service and remembrance of the guru; among Bāuls and Kartābhajās worship of the living guru as the human form of the Lord.

warnings.text: Kāl sends false teachers in the true guru's name.

name: Service (sevā)
method_summary: Voluntary service to the Master and community (Sant Mat: physical, financial and mental sevā at the Dera); among Bāuls feeding and serving sādhus (sādhu-sevā).

name: Singing the saints' songs (bhajan-kīrtan, Bāul gān)
method_summary: Singing the Sants' and Bāuls' songs in gatherings — as worship, as teaching and (for Bāuls) as practice and coded instruction; Ravidāsīs sing the Amritbāṇī; Kartābhajās the Bhāber Gīt.

name: Honest household livelihood
method_summary: Living as a householder by one's own craft (Kabīr the weaver, Ravidās the leatherworker, Dādū the cotton-carder), asking only for enough for the family and the visiting sādhu, rather than renouncing or begging.

name: Initiation into the Kabīr Panth
method_summary: Initiation by a mahant or ācārya with the giving of the Name and the kaṇṭhī necklace; in the Dharamdāsī line also the pān-parvānā; vows of vegetarianism and abstinence from intoxicants.

sources.ref: on the true Name and the pān-parvānā

name: The caukā rite (Dharamdāsī Kabīr Panth)
method_summary: A ritual on a square ground with coconut, betel leaves and lamps, performed by the ācārya for initiation and for the dead, by which souls receive the Name and the 'passport' past Kāl.
notes: Details from secondary accounts; low confidence.

name: Recitation and veneration of the Vāṇī
method_summary: Reading and singing the saint's collected utterances (Dādū Vāṇī; Amritbāṇī of Ravidās) in the panth's seats and gatherings, the book itself being honoured.

name: Surat-śabd yoga (the yoga of the sound current)
method_summary: Given only at initiation by a living master: the attention is withdrawn from the body and gathered at the eye centre by simran, held there by dhyān of the master's form, and joined to the inner sound (bhajan), which draws the soul up through the inner regions; practised daily (two and a half hours in the Beas line) with the vows.
signs_of_progress: attention gathering at the eye centre
inner light (stars, moon, sun) and the radiant form of the master
sounds of the regions (bell and conch first)

warnings.text: Without a living master and initiation the practice is not to be attempted; the lower centres and kuṇḍalinī are not to be worked on.
Inner lights and sounds are not to be sought for their own sake or spoken of; the disciple should not display powers.

equivalents.note: Both are absorption in the inner sound; surat-śabd yoga adds the master's form, the names and the regional cosmology.

name: Simran (Sant Mat)
method_summary: Mental repetition of the five (or other) names given at initiation, with attention at the eye centre, to still the mind and gather the attention.
notes: The names are confidential and not recorded.

name: Dhyān (contemplation of the master's form)
method_summary: Holding the attention at the eye centre by contemplating the living master's form, which later appears within as the radiant form.

name: Bhajan (listening to the sound current)
method_summary: Listening within to the inner sound (with the ears closed in some lines), selecting the sound from the right side and letting it draw the attention upward.

name: Nām-dān (initiation in Sant Mat)
method_summary: Initiation by the living master (or his representative), giving the names for simran and instruction in dhyān and bhajan, after the candidate has kept the vows for a period.

name: The Sant Mat vows
method_summary: Lacto-vegetarian diet (no meat, fish or eggs), abstention from alcohol and drugs, a moral life, and daily meditation — required of initiates.

warnings.text: Breaking the vows creates karma that holds the soul back.

name: The self-introspection diary
method_summary: Daily written record of failures in non-violence, truthfulness, chastity, love for all and selfless service, and of time given to meditation, introduced by Kirpal Singh.

name: Maharshi Mehi's graded practice
method_summary: Mental repetition (mānas jap), mental contemplation of form (mānas dhyān), fixing the gaze at a point (dṛṣṭi yoga) to open the inner light, and meditation on sound (nādānusandhān).

name: Worship of the human (mānuṣ bhajan)
method_summary: Serving and worshipping the divine in human beings, above all in the living guru, instead of images; in Kartābhajā the guru (Mahāśay) as the Kartā's presence.

name: Bāul initiation and instruction (dīkṣā and śikṣā)
method_summary: A first initiation (dīkṣā) by a guru with a mantra, and later instruction (śikṣā), often from a second guru, into the body practice; the teaching is given individually and kept secret.

warnings.text: The practice is not to be learned from books or songs without a guru.

name: Taking the garb (bhek; among Fakirs khilāphat)
method_summary: Initiation into mendicant life with the robe (ālkhāllā) and begging bowl, performed with a symbolic funeral of the old self in some lines; the fakiri counterpart is khilāphat.
notes: The 'symbolic funeral' detail is recalled from ethnographic reports with low confidence.

name: Song as practice (gān)
method_summary: Singing with the ektārā and dotārā as devotion, as teaching of the doctrine and as coded transmission of practice; the singer loses himself in the song of the Man.

name: Melās and sādhu-sevā
method_summary: Gathering at festivals — Joydeb-Kenduli at Pauṣ Saṃkrānti, Lalon's festival at Cheuṛiyā, the Kartābhajā Dol melā at Ghoshpara — for singing, teaching and feeding sādhus.

name: Bāul body practice (deha-sādhanā) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. A secret, guru-given practice of the couple and of the body's substances and breath, aimed at reversing the downward current and 'catching' the Man of the Heart in the body; recorded here only as its aim and the tradition's warnings — no method is given.

sources.ref: songs of the uncatchable Man and the tide

warnings.text: Only under a guru and after long preparation; without mastery of desire it leads to ruin and to the downward fall.
The practice is secret and must not be revealed to the unqualified.

name: Knowing the four moons (cāri candra bhed) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. A secret Bāul practice concerning four bodily substances ('moons'); recorded only by name, aim (reintegration of what the body emits) and the tradition's warnings — no method, substance handling or quantities.

warnings.text: Secret; never to be attempted without a guru; ruin follows otherwise.

name: Breath practice (dam) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. Coded Bāul teaching on the breath as the vehicle of the Man ('catch the thief in the house of air'); summary and warnings only, no retentions or counts.

warnings.text: Without the guru the seeker catches only wind.

name: The practice of the couple (Sahajiyā, Bāul) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. The ritual union of a man and a woman partner (sādhana-saṅginī), after long preparation through the stages of name, mantra and bhāva, in which the partners contemplate each other as Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā and aim to transform kāma into prema without the downward fall; recorded only as its aim and the texts' warnings.

sources.ref: on the difficulty of the path

warnings.text: The path is as hard as holding an elephant with a spider's thread; one must be near the fire and not burn.
Only the siddha, free of lust, is qualified; for others it is a fall into kāma.

name: Superimposition (āropa) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED context. Contemplating the svarūpa (Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā) in the rūpa of oneself and one's partner; the contemplative core of the couple's practice, recorded as doctrine only.

name: Name and mantra of the beginner (pravarta)
method_summary: At the beginner's stage the Sahajiyā relies on the Name and the mantra received from the guru, as in ordinary Vaiṣṇava practice, before any esoteric discipline.

name: Kartābhajā initiation
method_summary: Initiation by a Mahāśay with the sect's secret mantra, after which the disciple (barātī) worships the Kartā, pays dues and keeps the teaching hidden behind outward custom.
notes: The mantra is secret and not recorded.

name: The Dol festival at Ghoshpara
method_summary: At Dol Pūrṇimā (Holi) devotees gather at Ghoshpara at Satī Mā's shrine, bathe in the Himsāgar tank, tie threads at the pomegranate tree for healing and boons, and sing; many are possessed by bhāva.
